answer: Each agent must post a bond that is forfeited when independent audits catch duplicate identities or coordinated claims, while rewards vest only after a history of useful work. This makes a Sybil attack more than minting accounts: the attacker must lock real capital in every identity and risk losing it, then wait for each account to earn trust. A comet of fresh accounts cannot instantly drain the pool; even an oasis of cheap hosting leaves the ember of forfeited bonds burning on the attacker’s balance sheet.
